findings.why_it_matters: This replaces a guarantee that held unconditionally (an explicitly configured jinja2.Environment) with one that holds only through a deprecated compatibility shim in the installed starlette version plus an unpinned dependency range. If/when starlette removes the shim -- which its own deprecation warning signals is planned, and which the prior commit message confirms already broke this exact app once -- every templated page silently stops HTML-escaping context values, opening stored/reflected XSS across the dashboard, history, and settings templates with no other escaping layer to fall back on.

Confirmed current behavior is functionally safe (autoescape resolves True either way in installed starlette 0.52.1) — the finding is about reintroduced fragility/deprecation on an unpinned dependency, not an active vulnerability today.
No other FastAPI-mechanism issues found in this diff; it is a single-file, two-line-range change limited to template-engine construction.

findings.fix_hint: Restore the preconfigured jinja2.Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(...), autoescape=True) + Jinja2Templates(env=...) pattern from e11187e, or pin fastapi/starlette versions before reverting that fix.
findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e ("fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape"), whose message states Starlette deprecated/removed the `**env_options` passthrough on `Jinja2Templates`, risking that `autoescape=True` is silently not honored on newer Starlette releases. The revert goes back to `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)`, relying on that same deprecated kwarg-passthrough path (confirmed: in the currently installed starlette==0.52.1, `_create_env` still applies `env_options.setdefault("autoescape", True)`, so behavior is correct today, but it emits a DeprecationWarning). `pyproject.toml` pins `fastapi` with no version constraint, so a future `uv sync` can pull a Starlette release where this passthrough is removed outright, either hard-failing at import or silently dropping the explicit `autoescape=True` override this project's own CLAUDE.md treats as an absolute rule (never disable Jinja2 autoescaping).

findings.why_it_matters: Autoescaping is this project's only defense against unescaped HTML/Jinja2 output in the dashboard UI; silently undoing a previously-landed compatibility fix for it, on an unpinned dependency, is a latent forward-compatibility regression rather than a theoretical nitpick — it already broke once per the prior commit's own description.

findings.problem: The new constructor passes autoescape through Starlette’s deprecated **env_options path; the installed implementation explicitly warns to use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead. Escaping works today (a script payload rendered escaped), but the change replaces direct security configuration with a deprecated forwarding API. This matters because pyproject.toml leaves FastAPI unbounded and Dockerfile installs dependencies without uv.lock. Future compatibility and continued enforcement now depend on dependency behavior; no current XSS bypass was demonstrated.
